nodes.name: Branched Ru nanoparticle synthesis
nodes.procedure: Highly branched Ru nanoparticles with controllable crystallinity and surface facets have been generated by Tilley et al. using rational adjustment of the ratios of dodecylamine (DDA) surfactant to Ru precursor in the preparative process.
nodes.source_text: Highly branched Ru nanoparticles with controllable crystallinity and surface facets have been generated by Tilley et al. using rational adjustment of the ratios of dodecylamine (DDA) surfactant to Ru precursor in the preparative process.

nodes.name: Laser ablation in liquid
nodes.procedure: Du et al. took the advantage of the laser-ablation-in-liquid technique to create strain by introducing grain boundaries into activity enhanced Ru OER catalysts.
nodes.source_text: Du et al. took the advantage of the laser-ablation-in-liquid technique to create strain by introducing grain boundaries into activity enhanced Ru OER catalysts.

nodes.name: Single atom Ru on LDH
nodes.procedure: Single atom Ru anchored on the surface of CoFe-LDHs was prepared by Sun et al. using a simple two-step procedure involving co-precipitation of CoFe-LDHs and reduction of Ru precursor.
nodes.source_text: Single atom Ru anchored on the surface of CoFe-LDHs was prepared by Sun et al. using a simple two-step procedure involving co-precipitation of CoFe-LDHs and reduction of Ru precursor.

nodes.name: Ru-N-C single atom catalyst
nodes.procedure: A single-atom Ru–N–C catalyst was fabricated by Yao et al. by using incipient wetness impregnation of a Ru precursor into carbon support followed by pyrolysis.

unit_operations.name: Impregnation
unit_operations.procedure_snippet: incipient wetness impregnation of a Ru precursor into carbon support

nodes.source_text: A single-atom Ru–N–C catalyst was fabricated by Yao et al. by using incipient wetness impregnation of a Ru precursor into carbon support followed by pyrolysis.

nodes.name: Core-shell Ru-PtCu
nodes.procedure: Li et al. prepared a series of PtCux/Ptskin core–shell structures containing dispersed single-atom Ru (Ru1–PtxCuy) via acid or electrochemical etching of unstable Cu.
nodes.source_text: Li et al. prepared a series of PtCux/Ptskin core–shell structures containing dispersed single-atom Ru (Ru1–PtxCuy) via acid or electrochemical etching of unstable Cu.

nodes.name: Molten salt RuO2 nanosheets
nodes.procedure: Li et al. prepared defect-rich ultra-thin RuO2 nanosheets via a molten salt method involving directly mixing molten NaNO3 and RuCl3 at room temperature.
nodes.source_text: Li et al. prepared defect-rich ultra-thin RuO2 nanosheets via a molten salt method involving directly mixing molten NaNO3 and RuCl3 at room temperature.

nodes.name: Cr-Ru oxide from MOF
nodes.procedure: Chen et al. described a low Ru-content binary Cr–Ru oxide material derived from MIL-101 (Cr) (Fig. 7G), which shows a very low overpotential of 178 mV and maintains activity after the 10 h chronopotentiometry test at 10 mA cm-2 in acidic media.
